summary: Wrote a 6-phase plan that answers all five linked-repo questions by adopting sf1-engine's integration/project-link.md section 10 by citation, and found four of the five answers to be 'no change based on link state'. The one real gap is that sapience-remember.sh sends no project field at all, so the plan extends it with the same runtime project-key resolution sapience-publish.sh ko already implements (plain project key, never project_cid) plus the script's first test suite, and threads each ruling into a new indexed domain record, the write-path rule, and the three domain docs that own its reasoning. Three measured constraints shaped the phasing: EXTENSION.md sits at exactly 60 of its hard 60-line ceiling, index-entries.json line_count is a hard-failing coupled surface for every context edit, and the rule file's own 'exactly three' corpus figure is under-counted at a measured five. A concurrent sibling task holds per-repo-scoping.md in its declared file_scope this cycle, so that file is excluded from every phase and cited by heading instead.

artifacts.summary: 6 phases, 3 waves, 8 hours: rulings record and index wiring, sapience-remember.sh project tagging with its first test suite, rule file and domain-doc pointers, resolve-once postflight pass-through, line-neutral EXTENSION.md pointer, and a final deploy plus done-when verification phase.

user_decision.question: The linked-repo half of the done-when criterion cannot be exercised live here: this repository carries no .sapience/project.json, and creating a real binding is a permanent, undeletable write to your hosted vault. Verify against a fixture binding, or bind a real repository first?
options: Fixture-based verification — a scratch repo with a .sapience/project.json fixture and a stubbed GET /v1/people/projects, reusing the harness test-sapience-publish.sh already has; nothing reaches the live vault
Bind a real repository — you run sapience-project-bind.sh yourself to create a project, then the done-when criterion is confirmed end to end against the live API
user_decision.recommended: Fixture-based verification — a scratch repo with a .sapience/project.json fixture and a stubbed GET /v1/people/projects, reusing the harness test-sapience-publish.sh already has; nothing reaches the live vault
user_decision.obligation: Demonstrate that an orchestrated run in a repo carrying .sapience/project.json emits a KO body containing a resolved "project": "<key>" field and no project_cid key, while the same run in an unlinked repo emits a byte-identical body to today's.

next_action_hint: Run /orchestrate 678 to implement the plan. Phases 1 and 2 are independent and can start in either order.
